The presence of multiple targets, including Serine/threonine-protein kinase ICK and Oblonganoside C, indicates a broader role in the regulation of the NF-κB pathway, which is a well-known mediator of inflammation and immune responses. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible mechanism by which Ent-Gloeosteretriol exerts its effects, though the exact nature of its interaction with the target enzyme remains to be fully elucidated. The evidence supports a role in the NF-κB signaling cascade, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct involvement of Ent-Gloeosteretriol in the inhibition of this kinase subunit.
